chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Duke's voicings, and arrangers who know the instruments
summary: Duke and Strayhorn built unusual chords, and Benny Carter wrote saxophone parts that lay perfectly.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: See, like with Duke, he would play -- he used chords that ordinary arrangers wouldn't use. See, he would write notes and things that you would think

would be wrong, you know. We call them like--the guys call them Turkish nights and ninths Egyptians and twelves 6ths and things like --
And we'd call them all kind of ol' funny things, you know. It's all in the book.
Duke Ellington would write things, and he would put things together like he's building something, (inaudible) build a house -- this is good, I'll do this.
And that's what he would do with his music. He was just like -- him and Strayhorn was built for that.
They knew what an instrument could do. That's a good thing -- knowing what a trumpet can do and what a trumpet can't do.
What a trombone can do in a situation, and moving --
You got to know if the trombone can make this if the tempo is in. (Inaudible) or know if the saxophone --
This will come out clean if the tempo is up. Will the saxophone sound clean doing this, or will

You had all of his saxophone solos -- his saxophone things in here what's written. They all come out beautifully. You know (inaudible) all them doubled up choruses that Benny writes for the saxophones, (inaudible) them special things he write? They all come out, because they just lay there because he knows what the possibility -- what the instrument -- what you can do with that. It's so much you can do with a horn. So much you can do on a bass. So much a drummer can do, you know. Will it come out clean if you tell him to do so and so.
